details.text:
[assistant] {
  "score": 0.62,
  "gaps": [
    "Deliverables have named owners at the role level (Frontend Dev, QA Engineer) but no individual accountable owner per deliverable — 'game ui', 'game rules', and 'test checklist' are all assigned to the same abstract role without distinguishing ownership between the two frontend_dev modules, risking split-brain accountability on rule evaluation vs. UI.",
    "The sole declared risk 'rule evaluation bug' is echoed verbatim across feature-plan, feature-spec, and implementation-design without a concrete mitigation strategy attached — feature-spec only mentions 'regression defense via unit tests' in prose, but there is no explicit mitigation entry mapping risk → owner → verification mechanism → acceptance signal.",
    "Additional implicit risks surfaced in feature-spec (side-pot calculation, tie handling, straight/flush boundary, deck exhaustion, invalid action, rendering failure) are not registered in the Risks section of any document, so they have no owner, no mitigation, and no acceptance hook.",
    "Acceptance criteria in feature-spec are generic and non-observable: 'game ui의 핵심 기능이 구현된다', '검증 결과가 정리된다', '잔여 리스크와 후속 작업이 기록된다' — none define measurable signals (e.g., specific hand-ranking test vectors, deterministic seed replay, UI latency <100ms threshold already declared as NFR but not wired into acceptance).",
    "implementation-tasks.md has all nine tasks with `e2e_command: (needs_backfill)` — per the embedded Episode Hints rule 'e2e_command가 needs_backfill인 태스크는 PASS 처리 불가', the task list is structurally un-completable as-is and blocks the approval gate.",
    "Scope descriptions in feature-plan are tautological placeholders ('game ui을(를) 구현한다') rather than describing what the UI must show/allow, what rules must be evaluated (Texas Hold'em? 5-card draw? — variant is never specified), or what the test checklist must cover.",
    "Poker variant is never identified anywhere in the artifact. Feature-spec references phases 'preflop/flop/turn/river' which implies Texas Hold'em, but the goal, scope, and acceptance criteria never commit to a variant, leaving 'game rules' deliverable ambiguous.",
    "approval-gate.md has all version fields blank and `bug_fix_spec_version` / `bug_fix_spec_status` present even though this is a feature (not a bug fix) — schema mismatch against the declared `spec_type: feature`.",
    "feature-spec.md and implementation-design.md content is wrapped in a JSON code fence with an outer `{\"content\": \"...\"}` / `{\"document\": \"...\"}` envelope rather than being raw markdown — downstream readers expecting plain markdown will render the JSON scaffolding, and this inconsistency is not present in feature-plan.md or implementation-tasks.md.",
    "The Episode Hints block in feature-plan.md carries forward CLI/backend guidance that is irrelevant to a browser poker game ('CLI 키워드가 포함된 deliverable은 backend_dev에 배정한다'), suggesting template pollution rather than curated hints for this work item."
  ],
  "strengths": [
    "Four-document set (plan/spec/design/tasks) plus approval-gate is present and cross-linked via source_plan/source_spec/source_design chains.",
    "Non-functional requirements in feature-spec are concrete and testable where they exist: 100ms UI update, deterministic rule evaluation, offline-capable, ES2020+ target.",
    "Implementation-design captures a credible data model (GameState/Card/Player/GamePhase/Action) and commits to single-ownership of state in the rules module with unidirectional data flow to UI — this directly mitigates the 'rule evaluation bug' risk architecturally.",
    "Alternatives Considered section rejects four options (React/Vue, server-side rules, Canvas, monolithic module) with reasoning tied back to constraints (vanilla_js, offline, a11y, risk isolation).",
    "Local reference (docs/architecture.md # Modules) and web reference (Poker rules) are threaded consistently through all four documents as Evidence, preserving...
